question.text: TCS spot price is Rs. 3,800, the 2-month futures are trading at Rs. 3,780, and the cost of carry for 2 months is Rs. 50. The fair futures price should be Rs. 3,850. An arbitrageur would execute:

answer.text: Reverse cash and carry arbitrage: sell/short TCS in spot and buy TCS futures
Cash and carry arbitrage: buy TCS spot and sell futures
Buy both TCS spot and futures

explanation.text: The Logic: Step 1: Fair futures price = 3,800 + 50 = Rs. 3,850. Step 2: Actual futures price = Rs. 3,780. Step 3: Since actual futures price (Rs. 3,780) is below fair futures price (Rs. 3,850), execute reverse cash-and-carry by selling/shorting spot at Rs. 3,800 and buying futures at Rs. 3,780. At expiry, spot and futures converge; the arbitrageur captures roughly Rs. 70 after adjusting for the cost of carry. The Trap: Cash-and-carry (buy spot, sell futures) is the trade when futures are overpriced; here they are underpriced, so reverse cash-and-carry is correct. Buying both legs has no arbitrage payoff, and "no opportunity" ignores the Rs. 70 mispricing. Note: Step 3 of the explanation rewritten so the truncated "Since F(actual)" and "(3,780" inequalities are stated cleanly with both numerical values.
